'''Sara Snogerup Linse''' (born 30 April 1962) is a Swedish Professor of Biochemistry at [[Lund University]]. Her research considers the molecular mechanisms of protein self-assembly in [[Alzheimer's disease]]. She serves as Chair of the Committee for the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]]. She was awarded the 2019 [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] Women in Science Award.

== Early life and education ==
Linse grew up in the [[Oskarshamn Municipality]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sydsvenskan.se/2012-04-29/valorienterad-professor-pa-sprang|title=Välorienterad professor på språng|website=Sydsvenskan|date=29 April 2012 |language=sv|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref> Her parents are both botanists.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://network.febs.org/users/57741-febs-communications/posts/44752-sara-linse-i-really-love-working-in-the-lab|title=Sara Linse: "I really love working in the lab"|last=Network|first=FEBS|date=2019-03-03|website=FEBS Network|language=en|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref> She was thirteen years old when she first learned about proteins, and her high school teachers told her that there were still mysteries in establishing their structure – function properties.<ref name=":0" /> She studied [[chemical engineering]] at [[Lund University]] and [[Stanford University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.kth.se/en/om/fakta/fame/kths-stora-pris/2014-sara-snogerup-linse-1.496441|title=The KTH Great Prize 2014 awarded to Sara Snogerup Linse|website=KTH|language=en-UK|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref> She graduated in 1985 and started a doctorate at Lund University in [[physical chemistry]].<ref name=":1" /> She then came across another challenge in biochemistry: the interaction of proteins with nanoparticles.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
Linse was appointed to the faculty at Lund University in 1993, where she was promoted to Professor in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cmps.lu.se/biostruct/people/sara-linse/|title=Sara Snogerup Linse {{!}} Center for Molecular Protein Science, CMPS|website=www.cmps.lu.se|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref> Her research considers the molecular basis of neurological and metabolic diseases.<ref name=":1" />

When proteins spontaneously aggregate they can form fibrous clumps known as [[Amyloid|amyloids]]. [[Amyloid-beta peptide|Amyloid-beta peptides]] are associated with several neurological diseases, including [[Alzheimer's disease|Alzheimer's]] and [[Parkinson's disease]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://kaw.wallenberg.org/en/research/role-fats-protein-clumps|title=The role of fats in protein clumps|website=Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation|language=en|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref> Linse has demonstrated that the process of nucleation and growth of amyloid-beta peptide occurs in two phases; first the amyloid fibrils form and then monomers nucleate on the surface.<ref name=":0" /> This second nucleation event gives rise to most of the neuronal toxicity.<ref name=":0" /> Linse was supported by the [[Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation]] to investigate the role of fat in protein self-assembly.<ref name=":2" /> Fat molecules (lipids) are often present when aggregations are formed, but the majority of research considers how proteins attach to the [[cell membrane]].<ref name=":2" />

Her research makes use of a variety of analytical tools to study protein amyloid formation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fluidic.com/news-and-events/news/sara-linse-fluidity-one-w-FEBS2019/|title=Professor Sara Linse presents new data on protein interactions in Alzheimer's disease using the Fluidity One-W at FEBS 2019|website=www.fluidic.com|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cambridgenetwork.co.uk/news/professor-sara-linse-presents-new-data-protein-interactions-alzheimer%E2%80%99s-disease-using-fluidity|title=Professor Sara Linse presents new data on protein interactions in Alzheimer's disease using the Fluidity One-W at FEBS 2019 {{!}} Cambridge Network|website=www.cambridgenetwork.co.uk|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref> In 2020 Linse and co-workers announced a mathematical model that could be used to describe the chemical reactions that are responsible for the fibroid aggregation associated with [[Alzheimer's disease biomarkers|Alzheimer's]] disease.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2020/01/200128114705.htm|title=New mathematical model for amyloid formation: Equations describe chemical reactions responsible for the formation of protein aggregates associated with illnesses like Alzheimer's disease|website=ScienceDaily|language=en|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref>

=== Awards and honours ===
Her awards and honours include:

* 2004 Elected to the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":1" />
* 2007 [[National Academy of Sciences]] Cozzarelli Prize<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pnas.org/page/about/cozzarelli-prize|title=The Cozzarelli Prize: 2019 Call for Nominations {{!}} PNAS|website=www.pnas.org|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www8.nationalacademies.org/onpinews/newsitem.aspx?RecordID=02132008|title=PNAS Announces 2007 Cozzarelli Prize Recipients|website=www8.nationalacademies.org|language=en|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref> 
* 2011 [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]] Distinguished Woman in Chemistry prize<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iupac.org/100/stories/iupac-distinguished-women-in-chemistry/|title=IUPAC Distinguished Women in Chemistry|website=IUPAC 100|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref>
* 2012 Joined the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] Committee<ref name=":1" />
* 2014 [[KTH Royal Institute of Technology]] Great Prize<ref name=":1" />
* 2019 [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] Women in Science Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.febs.org/news/sara-linse-receives-the-2019-febs-embo-women-in-science-award/|title=FEBS {{!}} Sara Linse receives the 2019 FEBS {{!}} EMBO Women in Science Award {{!}} News|website=www.febs.org|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref>

=== Selected publications ===
Her publications include:

* {{Cite journal|last=Linse|first=Sara|date=2007-02-13|title=Understanding the nanoparticle–protein corona using methods to quantify exchange rates and affinities of proteins for nanoparticles|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=104|issue=7|pages=2050–2055|doi=10.1073/pnas.0608582104|pmid=17267609|pmc=1892985|doi-access=free}}
* {{Cite journal|last=Linse|first=Sara|date=2007-05-22|title=Nucleation of protein fibrillation by nanoparticles|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=104|issue=21|pages=8691–8696|doi=10.1073/pnas.0701250104|pmid=17485668|pmc=1866183|doi-access=free|bibcode=2007PNAS..104.8691L }}
* {{Cite journal|last=Linse|first=Sara|date=2007-10-31|title=The nanoparticle–protein complex as a biological entity; a complex fluids and surface science challenge for the 21st century|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=134|pages=167–174|doi=10.1016/j.cis.2007.04.021|pmid=17574200}}

Linse publishes children's books with her partner Kyrre Thalberg.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.embo.org/news/articles/2019/i-really-love-working-in-the-lab|title=I really love working in the lab|last=EMBO|website=EMBO|date=18 February 2019 |language=en-gb|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref> These have included ''Draksommar'',<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Thalberg|first1=Kyrre|title=Draksommar|last2=Snogerup Linse|first2=Sara|date=2012|publisher=Atremi|isbn=978-91-7527-021-0|location=Mjölby|language=sv|oclc=939732854}}</ref> ''Kjetil och Jostein'',<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Thalberg|first1=Kyrre|title=Kjetil och Jostein|last2=Snogerup Linse|first2=Sara|date=2013|publisher=Atremi|isbn=978-91-7527-057-9|location=Mjölby|language=sv|oclc=940620266}}</ref> ''Höst i Drakbergen'',<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Thalberg|first1=Kyrre|title=Höst i Drakbergen|last2=Snogerup Linse|first2=Sara|date=2014|publisher=Atremi|isbn=978-91-7527-095-1|location=Mjölby|language=sv|oclc=941226080}}</ref> ''Prins Pralin åker buss'',<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Thalberg|first1=Kyrre|title=Prins Pralin åker buss|last2=Snogerup Linse|first2=Sara|date=2013|publisher=Atremi|isbn=978-91-7527-030-2|location=Mjölby|language=sv|oclc=940304639}}</ref> and ''Karnevalen i Brind''.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Snogerup Linse|first1=Sara|title=Karnevalen i Brind.|last2=Thalberg|first2=Kyrre|last3=Snogerup|first3=Sara|last4=Thalberg|first4=Kyrre|last5=Snogerup|first5=Sara|last6=Thalberg|first6=Kyrre|date=2019|isbn=978-91-7527-255-9|language=sv|oclc=1111658695}}</ref> She is also [[2018 World Masters Orienteering Championships|2018 World Masters Orienteering Champion]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eventor.orienteering.org/Athletes/Details/3489|title=IOF Eventor - Sara Snogerup Linse|website=eventor.orienteering.org|language=en|access-date=2020-02-16}}</ref>
